According to a Right to Information (RTI) response from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal, of the appeals decided, 75,443 resulted in voters being included in the electoral roll, while 7,339 resulted in exclusion. In other words, 91.13% of the decided appeals resulted in inclusion. These voters were not allowed to cast votes during the recent West Bengal assembly elections. The RTI response was provided in response to Congress MP Isha Khan Choudhury's application. He had sought information on the appeals arising from the SIR exercise. The figures provide a district-wise and gender-wise picture of the electoral rolls alongside the status of the appellate process. The response shows that 37,27,838 appeals, or 97.83% of the total, are still pending, with only 1 in every 46 appeals decided so far. items.title: ‘Delhi became the source of all real knowledge’: How TV newsrooms pushed regional reporters aside
items.summary: Today, it feels as if the role of the reporter on a TV news channel has shrunk compared to the days when we started out. There are, of course, honourable exceptions, reporters who continue to produce high-quality work that makes an impact. But too many of the new crop of reporters deliver just what is expected of them—which is not enough in terms of originality and high standards. What is expected can, however, be too much in terms of working hours, number of lives or ‘OB’s. But with little reward in terms of the feeling of a responsible and important job well done, burnout is faster for the young reporter today. The initial thrill of coming on air and having access to the powerful can last a while, but is not enough to sustain them for a long career. A young reporter I worked with was very clear when she said, ‘I don’t want to be doing this when I am thirty!’ I had been on the job for more years than she had been alive, but I could understand where she was coming from. The devaluation of the field reporter has been a huge blow to the television news industry in India. I am talking about the genuine, around-the-year ground reporter—not the times when a Star Anchor makes the effort

items.title: NLSIU cancels convocation for 2026 graduating batch
items.summary: National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru has cancelled its convocation for the graduating batch of 2026. On August 3, the administration had emailed the graduating students stating that the annual convocation would be held on September 12. However, a notice dated August 27 has now announced that no convocation would be held due to "unavoidable circumstances" and that students would be conferred their degrees in absentia . "Despite our collective best efforts, due to unavoidable circumstances, we are unable to hold the 34th Annual Convocation. All graduating students will be conferred their degrees in absentia after due approvals by the Governing Bodies," the notice said. Students may elect to receive their certificates by courier or collect them at campus, it added. The University will share a new form and the process with all graduating students to choose their preferred option. The decision comes close on the heels of opposition by students and alumni to Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra and Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant attending the convocation. items.title: Can IP suits be instituted anywhere because products available online pan-India? Delhi HC larger bench to decide
items.summary: Companies cannot institute intellectual property suits virtually anywhere in the country merely because products or advertisements are accessible online, the Delhi High Court recently said [HUL Vs Kwick Living]. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhan i opined that internet cannot become a basis for companies to claim territorial jurisdiction anywhere in India for instituting IP suits. He made the observation while referring to a larger bench three questions concerning territorial jurisdiction in intellectual property disputes, particularly those involving online transactions. “ It is extremely important to point-out that, by reason of the advent of the internet and the accessibility of goods at any remote location via the world-wide-web, the principles of law in relation to territorial jurisdiction of courts cannot be so diluted or be made so vague that a corporation could sue in just about any location within the country .” The Court added that such an approach would throw the very concept of territorial jurisdiction of courts to the winds. items.title: More than 1,300 are missing in Nepal and Tibet after catastrophic floods caused by glacial collapse
items.summary: Rescue teams were searching for hundreds of missing people along the Nepal-China border after a catastrophic and deadly torrent of floods and mud swept through several communities a day earlier following a glacial collapse. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority in Nepal said 826 people were missing and the death toll from the country’s flash floods rose to 165 on Thursday. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV separately reported that 260 of the 558 missing people in Tibet were foreigners and two villagers were rescued. At least three people were killed as of Thursday morning, it said. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. A map showing districts impacted by a flash flood in Nepal.
